analyzed_vuln.description: Heap buffer overflow is caused by allocating the conversion buffer with mp_radix_size() but calling mp_toradix() with an invalid radix value (fuzzer-controlled uint8_t). In the SP math build, unsupported radix values are effectively treated as hex conversion in sp_toradix/sp_tohex, which can write more bytes than the size computed for that invalid radix (observed 1-byte allocation, then 1-byte OOB write at sp_tohex). Crash occurs in sp_tohex at wolfssl-sp-math-all/wolfcrypt/src/sp_int.c:12515.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Data flow: fuzz input -> Bignum::GetPtr() optionally calls baseConversion() -> baseConversion() picks arbitrary base from datasource -> calls mp_radix_size(mp, base, &size), allocates exactly size bytes, then calls mp_toradix(mp, str, base). Trigger requires convert=true and a base value that leads to under-sized output buffer (e.g., invalid radix producing tiny size) while mp_toradix still emits hex digits, causing write past allocation.
